subject: Request: One-time quarterly invoicing + deferred remit concession for Solstice Labs
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: deal-desk@redwood.com; karthik_iyer@redwood.com; marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: One-time quarterly invoicing + deferred remit concession for Solstice Labs

Team —

Quick ask: Solstice Labs (prospect -> pilot underway) is requesting a one-time deviation from standard monthly Net-30 billing. Their finance team runs on fiscal quarters and has asked for quarterly invoices with Net-90 on the first two invoices to align cashflows across their product lines. Key facts:

- Expected ARR if pilot converts: ~$1.2M annualized
- Initial committed pilot spend (first 3 months): ~$45k
- They will provide a PO (attached) and have requested a 5% early-pay discount if they can commit to a quarterly prepay on next year's rollout
- Timeline sensitivity: procurement wants terms confirmed by 11/24 to include in their December board packet

Risks called out by Finance are known: longer DSO and collections exposure. Asked options here: temporary quarterly cadence for first 2 quarters (Q1/Q2 2027) with the plan to revert to monthly Net-30 thereafter; or Net-60 with a small prepay.

Attached: Q4 proposal PDF and their PO they just sent. Requesting Finance / Deal Desk review and exec signoff if needed. Happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com

Attachments: Q4-Proposal_Solstice.pdf, PO_Solstice_20261115.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com; marissa_cole@redwood.com; deal-desk@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: One-time quarterly invoicing + deferred remit concession for Solstice Labs

+1 from me — Solstice is strategic for our Telco vertical (they have channel partners that would expand distribution). A few notes to add context:

- They are asking for the cadence because multiple business units consolidate at quarter end; they cannot accept monthly invoices to centralize vendor payments
- CFO (Amit Rao) did explicitly say they cannot prepay the full quarter; PO in place covers services but not payment timing
- Customer is sensitive to any escrow or L/C requirement — it slows procurement considerably

Ask: Finance, can you provide the minimal set of controls to make this acceptable? If Legal needs to sign a specific concession with a rev-rec clause, we'll get it signed ASAP. If we need an executive exception, flag it here so we can coordinate approval.

—Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com; karthik_iyer@redwood.com; jonas_weber@redwood.com; deal-desk@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: One-time quarterly invoicing + deferred remit concession for Solstice Labs

Thanks for the context. I ran a quick exposure calc (attached) — baseline risk for two quarters of Net-90 on a ~$45k pilot is manageable, but exposure scales if they roll to full ARR. Options I can support without exec signoff:

1) Net-60 for first two invoices + customer provides an approved PO and ACH authorization (standard credit hold monitoring)
2) Net-90 for first two invoices but require a 25% partial payment on the first invoice or a signed irrevocable bank guarantee (we've used this with three enterprise customers)
3) Approve quarterly invoicing cadence operationally (generate one consolidated invoice per quarter) while keeping payment terms Net-30 — customer pays within 30 days of the consolidated invoice; this is sometimes easier for procurement\/AP teams to accept with internal processing windows

If Sales wants purely Net-90 + no prepay/guarantee, I will need executive signoff from Revenue and CFO to accept the DSO increase and to set a credit watch. Please advise which of the above aligns with the customer's constraints.

Marissa Cole
Finance Manager, Revenue Operations
Attachments: risk_calc.xlsx

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com; karthik_iyer@redwood.com; jonas_weber@redwood.com; Evelyn Park <evelyn@solsticelabs.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: One-time quarterly invoicing + deferred remit concession for Solstice Labs

Marissa — thanks, that's helpful. To clarify from the customer side: they cannot do a 25% prepay given internal treasury rules, and an L/C would add ~6–8 weeks to procurement. Their preference is either option (2) without the guarantee or option (3) with Net-30 on the consolidated invoice — but procurement insists on the consolidated quarterly invoice coming through (not monthly).

Given that, Sales is asking for a short-term, time-boxed executive concession: allow quarterly consolidated invoicing with Net-90 on the first two quarterly invoices (so DSO spike only during pilot ramp), and we put them on credit watch with stronger collection SLAs (30/60/90 escalations) before any full rollout. We will capture this in an addendum: temporary deviation valid for Q1 and Q2 2027; revert to monthly Net-30 after that unless a committed annual contract is signed.

If we get approval for that path, I'll confirm with the customer and get the signed addendum and PO on file.

Naomi

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com; marissa_cole@redwood.com; karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: One-time quarterly invoicing + deferred remit concession for Solstice Labs

I reviewed the ask and the upside. Approve a controlled exception with conditions. Executive decision: APPROVE Net-90 for the first two quarterly invoices only subject to the following binding conditions — all must be satisfied before the first invoice is posted.

1) Customer must provide a signed PO (received) and an internal AP contact with ACH mandate on file.
2) Finance to place Solstice on "credit watch" and configure 30/60/90 escalation emails to collections and AE.
3) Revenue holdback: Redwood will retain 15% of each invoice amount as reserve, released after the second quarter upon verification of usage and payment compliance. This is to mitigate revenue recognition risk and collections exposure.
4) Legal to add a 2-quarter temporary addendum (auto-reverts to standard terms unless extended by Sales + Revenue approval).

Karthik — Naomi, move forward with customer communication that we have conditional approval. Marissa — please confirm when you have the controls and add the reserve on the billing system. If Legal needs an exec note, I will sign.

Jonas Weber
VP, Revenue Operations
jonas_weber@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com; naomi_feldman@redwood.com; karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 17:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: One-time quarterly invoicing + deferred remit concession for Solstice Labs

Acknowledged and will implement the controls today. Action items I will complete before billing:

- Set credit watch and configure 30/60/90 escalation workflow
- Create billing schedule for quarterly consolidated invoice (first invoice target: 2027-01-10)
- Apply 15% reserve hold to each invoice line item in our billing system and mark for release conditionals
- Loop Legal for the 2-quarter addendum (please attach any customer language Naomi wants us to include)

I'll confirm once done and post a note to the HubSpot deal record.

Marissa
Finance Manager, Revenue Operations
